named-executor-what-you-agreed-to-uk.title: Named as an executor: first decisions in the UK
named-executor-what-you-agreed-to-uk.dek: Check the national estate process, your options about acting, and the duties that come before distributions, with records for questions and decisions.
named-executor-what-you-agreed-to-uk.metaDescription: Check the national estate process, your options about acting, and the duties that come before distributions, with records for questions and decisions.

paragraphs: If you are named executor in a UK will, first identify the applicable national estate process, decide whether you can act and preserve the information needed to administer the estate. Do not assume one UK-wide form or that finding your name lets you complete every transaction. Probate in England and Wales, Scottish confirmation and Northern Ireland procedures differ.

You may have agreed years earlier without seeing the eventual property, debts or family situation. Before promising beneficiaries a payment date, establish what must be done and whether you need professional help. This is general administration guidance, not legal advice or a complete procedure for every UK estate.

body.heading: Before substantive administration
items: Find the original will and amendments, identify every named executor and check any substitute appointment. Preserve documents rather than annotating or dividing them.
Establish the relevant jurisdiction and ask about cross-border property or domicile uncertainty. Do not select a court only because it is nearest to you.
List urgent care, security, insurance and business issues. Ask who may handle them while authority and grant requirements are being established.
If you do not want to act, get advice about your options before taking substantive steps. Disclose anything already done; do not guess whether it counts as administration.
Create an initial asset, ownership and liability list. Note unknowns instead of assuming every pension, policy and joint account falls into the distributable estate.
Keep correspondence, expenses and decisions dated. Do not mix funds or promise an inheritance before claims, tax and authority questions are understood.

paragraphs: [Open the free uk executor role and jurisdiction record](/guides/print/library/named-executor-what-you-agreed-to-uk.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: Three UK estate routes distinguish England and Wales probate, Scottish confirmation and Northern Ireland probate.
body.caption: Similar terminology does not make the procedures interchangeable.

body.heading: Use the correct official route
rows: GOV.UK applying for probate and estate-administration guidance.
That every estate needs a grant, or that renunciation and power reserved are the same.
Scottish Courts guidance on dealing with a deceased estate and confirmation.
That England/Wales probate forms or inheritance rules apply.
NI Direct probate guidance and its own application process.
That the England/Wales procedure for reserving power transfers unchanged.

body.heading: Deciding not to act needs the right procedure
paragraphs: For England and Wales, [GOV.UK explains options where there is a will](https://www.gov.uk/applying-for-probate/if-theres-a-will). Where more than one executor is named, power reserved can retain the ability to apply later; renunciation gives up the right to apply through its stated process. These are different decisions with different effects. Check the current form and conditions rather than copying a letter found online.

[NI Direct](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/probate) describes its own reserved-power and renunciation position. In Scotland, ask a Scottish solicitor or the relevant court about your circumstances rather than using an England/Wales form. If you have already started dealing with the estate or a grant has issued, get advice before assuming you can simply withdraw.

Helping with immediate funeral or safety arrangements is not a reason to make your own legal judgment about whether you have committed to the full role. Describe the exact acts to an adviser. If another executor will act, agree who will preserve records and communicate while the formal position is settled.

body.heading: Invented example: two executors with different capacity
paragraphs: A will names two siblings. One can manage paperwork now; the other is caring for a child and cannot take on routine administration. They identify the England/Wales route and ask about applying with power reserved to the second executor rather than describing both siblings as having renounced.

Before choosing, they check whether either has already taken substantive steps and what notices or written communication are needed. If the same family were dealing with a Scottish estate, they would not copy this option automatically. The example demonstrates a question to ask, not a recommendation for every joint appointment.

body.alt: An executor timeline separates role and authority, asset identification, liabilities and final accounting.
body.caption: A grant does not automatically make the bank balance available for distribution.

body.heading: The role lasts beyond obtaining a grant
paragraphs: [GOV.UK's estate overview](https://www.gov.uk/probate-estate) describes responsibility for estate assets during administration. The work can include identifying property, establishing values and ownership, collecting assets through the appropriate process, dealing with liabilities and tax, then distributing and accounting. Obtaining a grant is a milestone, not proof the estate is ready to pay out.

[Scottish Courts' confirmation guide](https://www.scotcourts.gov.uk/taking-action/dealing-with-a-deceaseds-estate-in-scotland/guide-to-dealing-with-a-deceaseds-estate-in-scotland/) explains the estate inventory in its own system. Do not reuse an informal family estimate where the process requires a supported value. Seek suitable valuation or tax advice for property, a business or uncertain ownership.

body.heading: Separate debts, tax and beneficiaries' expectations
paragraphs: Record known bills, possible claims and the tax questions requiring professional review. Do not pay creditors simply in order of arrival or distribute the apparent bank balance without reserves and the required checks. If the estate may be insolvent, stop and ask about the applicable priority rules. A friendly family agreement cannot necessarily remove another claimant's rights.

The deceased person's final tax position and income arising during administration can be different issues. Ask which information HMRC and the relevant estate process require for the date of death and estate circumstances. This guide deliberately does not supply a universal tax threshold, clearance period or deadline.

Ask a solicitor about creditor notices and any applicable protective process before relying on them. Such notices are not a universal UK immunity from every claim. Disputed entitlement, dependants' claims, foreign assets, missing funds, capacity concerns or plans for an executor to buy estate property need particular care.

body.heading: Ask before taking the next step

items.line: I am named executor, the estate appears to involve [assets and debts], and these actions have already happened: [facts]. Which national process applies, can I step aside, and what must be protected now?
I am confirming authority, ownership and the estate's liabilities. I cannot promise a distribution date yet. I will update you when [specific information] is confirmed.

body.heading: Agree help, costs and a manageable record
paragraphs: If using a professional, ask who is the client, what work is included, how fees are calculated, who authorizes extra work and what you remain responsible for. Do not assume every proposed expense can be reimbursed from the estate without question. Keep the engagement and supporting invoices.

Record the date, transaction, amount, evidence and reason for every estate payment or receipt. Keep an issues list with an owner and next action rather than relying on messages between relatives. Beneficiaries need accurate progress information, but a fixed completion promise is unreliable where sales, tax, claims or disputes control the timetable.

For registration and immediate notifications, use [the UK first-steps guide](/guides/what-to-do-when-a-parent-dies-uk). For this decision, the main outcome is simpler: you know the jurisdiction, your intended role, the evidence of authority needed and which action cannot safely wait.

items.q: Does agreeing during their lifetime mean I must act?
items.a: Not necessarily, but you should establish the correct national procedure and disclose what you have already done. Options and consequences differ between declining before acting and leaving after substantive administration or a grant. Get advice before signing a renunciation or assuming silence transfers the role to someone else.

items.q: Is power reserved the same as renunciation?
items.a: No. In England and Wales, power reserved can preserve the right to apply later where other executors are applying, while renunciation gives up that right through the stated process. Northern Ireland has its own position and Scotland uses a different system. Verify the applicable route before choosing forms.

items.q: Can I pay beneficiaries once probate is granted?
items.a: A grant does not itself resolve debts, tax, disputed ownership or other claims. Check the estate's liabilities, required procedures and reserves before distributing. If there is uncertainty or pressure to pay early, seek advice and explain which issue is outstanding rather than treating the grant date as an automatic payout deadline.

named-executor-what-you-agreed-to-uk.seoTitle: Named as an executor: first decisions (UK)

named-executor-what-you-agreed-to.title: Named executor of a will: first decisions (US)
named-executor-what-you-agreed-to.dek: Understand nomination, court authority and estate duties before moving money, and check the local process if you cannot accept the executor role.
named-executor-what-you-agreed-to.metaDescription: Understand nomination, court authority and estate duties before moving money, and check the local process if you cannot accept the executor role.

paragraphs: Being named executor in a US will nominates you for estate administration; it does not automatically prove you have authority to transact. First decide whether you can serve, locate the will, identify the applicable probate or alternative process, and protect urgent interests without distributing property. If appointed, you manage estate duties rather than simply hand out inheritances.

Your name may appear in a document written years ago, before the family circumstances or your own capacity changed. You can ask what the job involves before promising to do it. This is a first-decision guide, not a state-specific probate manual, tax opinion or instruction to take actions beyond your authority.

body.heading: Before accepting transactions as routine
items: Locate the original will and any amendments. Identify co-nominees and alternates without deciding contested validity yourself.
Ask the relevant court about will-deposit duties, the appointment process, any small-estate alternative, required notices and urgent deadlines.

If unsure about serving, ask about declining before undertaking substantive administration. Explain exactly what you have already done rather than assuming one call either commits you or means nothing.
List immediate care, security, insurance or business-continuity concerns and ask who may lawfully handle them pending appointment.
Gather an initial map of assets, debts and ownership. Separate possible estate assets from joint, beneficiary-designated or trust assets needing another route.
Keep a dated decision and expense record from the start. Do not mix estate receipts with your own spending or make informal promises of distributions.

paragraphs: [Open the free us executor acceptance and authority check](/guides/print/library/named-executor-what-you-agreed-to.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: An executor sequence separates nomination, local procedure, documented authority and administration.
body.caption: The correct local process comes before ordinary estate transactions.

body.heading: Authority comes before ordinary estate transactions
paragraphs: In New York, [the court appoints the fiduciary](https://www.nycourts.gov/help/when-someone-dies/fiduciary-estate). The court document and permitted powers matter when dealing with institutions. Other states use their own processes and terminology. Ask which evidence each institution needs rather than presenting the will as a universal withdrawal authorization.

A power of attorney used during life is not a substitute for the post-death estate process. Do not impersonate the deceased person online, transfer a balance into your own account, or sign a sale because a family member says the will makes it yours anyway. Ask about necessary temporary authority if a genuine urgent transaction cannot wait.

body.heading: The work after the proper authority is established
columns: Decision that must not be skipped
rows: Inventory, ownership evidence and secure records.
Which assets belong in this administration?
Supported date-of-death values and specialist advice where needed.
Is the value documented rather than guessed?
A schedule of notices, returns, liabilities and reserves.
Which rules, priorities and deadlines actually apply?
Approved accounting, receipts and closure evidence.
Have claims, taxes, restrictions and required approvals been resolved?

body.heading: Invented example: a house, an account and an old pension
paragraphs: A nominated executor finds a house with a mortgage, one sole-name bank account and a retirement statement naming an administrator. They record these as leads. They do not assume the pension is part of the probate estate, or promise the house to one sibling before checking ownership and the will.

They ask the court about appointment, the bank about required documents and the plan administrator about the benefit-claim route. The first useful output is a verified map and next-action list, not a total inheritance figure. If a mortgage or insurer needs immediate contact, they gather instructions and document who has authority for the action requested.

body.alt: An executor record separates assets, liabilities, transactions and decisions with supporting evidence.
body.caption: A clear record supports review; it does not replace required legal steps.

body.heading: Separate the deceased person's tax from estate administration
paragraphs: The [IRS administrator guidance](https://www.irs.gov/individuals/responsibilities-of-an-estate-administrator) distinguishes obligations involving the deceased person and the estate. Ask a qualified tax adviser which federal and state filings are required, who signs them and when. Do not assume that a small estate means no final income-tax work, or confuse estate income tax with estate transfer tax.

Where an estate identification number is needed, use the [official IRS EIN route](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/get-an-employer-identification-number), not an unsolicited paid intermediary. An EIN is not proof of court appointment. Ask the bank what authority and identification it requires before opening an estate account; do not create accounts merely to feel the process has started.

body.heading: Personal liability is about duties, not inheriting every debt
paragraphs: The [FTC explains that estate debts are generally paid from estate assets](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/debts-and-deceased-relatives), with exceptions affecting some personal obligations. An estate representative can also create problems by mishandling legal duties. Do not pay creditors in the order they call or distribute funds on the assumption that later claims can simply be ignored.

If liabilities may exceed assets, stop before paying or distributing and seek probate advice about priorities. The same applies to disputed wills, taxes you cannot assess, a business, foreign property, missing funds or a sale to yourself or another relative. A lawyer's fees, compensation and reimbursement arrangements should be agreed and checked against the will, law and any required approval; estate payment is not an unlimited guarantee.

body.heading: Questions before you commit

items.line: I am nominated in the will and have not established transaction authority. Which steps preserve the estate, what appointment route applies, and what deadlines need attention now?
I do not think I can undertake administration. These are the actions I have already taken: [facts]. What is the correct local procedure for declining or, if already appointed, seeking release?

body.heading: Give the family process updates, not premature promises
paragraphs: Record receipts, values, provider responses and the basis for decisions. Agree a practical update channel so beneficiaries know what is confirmed and what remains unresolved. Being both a beneficiary and nominated executor does not remove the need to handle competing interests carefully.

Do not promise completion in a set number of weeks. Court processing, claims, tax questions, sales and disputes can each control the pace. Track actual milestones and ask for help with a specific blocked decision. Hiring help does not automatically transfer all your responsibilities; clarify who is doing what in writing.

items.q: Do I have to serve because the will names me?
items.a: Nomination does not mean you must silently take the job on. Ask the relevant court or probate attorney how to decline and explain anything you have already done. If you have been appointed, stepping down requires the proper release or replacement process; do not simply stop responding or hand the file to a relative.

items.q: Can I distribute money once I find the will?
items.a: Not simply because the will has been found. Authority, ownership, creditor procedures, tax obligations and any required approval must be checked. A distribution that seems obvious to the family can still be premature. Preserve the money and get advice before paying inheritances or moving estate funds into personal accounts.

items.q: Does the executor personally pay the estate's debts?
items.a: Not automatically from personal funds, but personal obligations and mistakes in administration can change the position. Ask about responsibility before making promises or payments. If the estate may be insolvent, get advice about claim priorities and required procedure instead of paying whichever creditor applies the most pressure.

what-to-do-when-a-parent-dies-uk.title: What to do when a parent dies in the UK
what-to-do-when-a-parent-dies-uk.dek: Check the correct registration route, arrange immediate care, and separate Tell Us Once from the banks and insurers you still need to contact.
what-to-do-when-a-parent-dies-uk.metaDescription: Check the correct registration route, arrange immediate care, and separate Tell Us Once from the banks and insurers you still need to contact.

paragraphs: When a parent dies in the UK, first follow the care team's or emergency service's instructions, check anyone who relies on them, and identify the registration route for the nation where the death occurred. England and Wales use the medical-examiner process before registration; Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own rules.

The first difficulty may be not knowing which call is yours to make. Keep one note with the hospital or GP contact, registrar, funeral director and the person coordinating family information. This guide helps with the first fortnight; it does not determine inheritance, replace legal advice or cover every death abroad.

body.heading: Start with people and immediate risks
items: For a hospital or care-home death, ask staff who will explain verification, certification and release arrangements. For an expected home death, use the care plan or GP contact instructions. If there is an emergency or uncertainty about whether the person has died, call 999.
Arrange support for any surviving dependent, and care for pets. Check whether someone needs food, medication access, keys or transport tonight.
Secure the property and address urgent hazards. Ask the home insurer what changes if it will be unoccupied; do not assume an ordinary household policy continues unchanged.
Find any funeral wishes or prepaid plan before buying arrangements. You can speak to a funeral director while official paperwork is pending; permission for burial or cremation is a separate issue.
Locate the will and the solicitor's details. Keep the original intact and avoid promising that you can distribute property immediately.

paragraphs: [Open the free uk first-fortnight contact and registration record](/guides/print/library/what-to-do-when-a-parent-dies-uk.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: Three national registration routes distinguish England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
body.caption: The UK does not have one interchangeable registration process.

body.heading: Registration: use the right national instructions
rows: Wait for medical-examiner confirmation that registration can proceed.
Register within five days of confirmation, including weekends and bank holidays; contact the registrar immediately if more time is needed.
Contact a Scottish registration office; the registrar needs the medical certificate.
Official Scottish guidance says within eight days of death where possible; ask about referrals or delays.
Follow NI Direct and the district registrar's instructions.
Register within five days unless referred to the coroner; ask the registrar if there is a delay.

body.heading: Why waiting for confirmation is not missing your task
paragraphs: In England and Wales, the [GOV.UK registration guidance](https://www.gov.uk/after-a-death/register-the-death) says to wait for the medical examiner's office to confirm that you can register. Do not count five days from the death and assume you have failed while certification is pending. Write down when confirmation arrives and contact the register office if the timing cannot be met.

Use [Scottish registration guidance](https://www.mygov.scot/register-death) and [NI Direct](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/registering-death-district-registrar) for those nations rather than extending the England/Wales process across the UK. A coroner or procurator fiscal referral changes the practical sequence; ask the office handling the case which document is available and what can proceed.

body.heading: Invented example: a hospital death in Leeds
paragraphs: A parent dies on Sunday. On Monday the daughter asks the hospital for the medical-examiner office contact, checks the house and talks to a funeral director about provisional arrangements. She does not invent a Wednesday registration deadline. When the examiner's office confirms registration can proceed, she records the date and contacts the registrar within the applicable window.

Meanwhile, her brother asks banks and pension providers which evidence they need. He records the answers without moving money or cancelling essential household cover. Splitting information gathering from estate transactions lets relatives help without implying they all have authority.

body.alt: A bereavement record separates government notification, private providers and outstanding follow-ups.
body.caption: A submitted government notification does not complete private bereavement administration.

body.heading: Tell Us Once does not tell everyone
paragraphs: The registrar can provide the reference for [Tell Us Once](https://www.gov.uk/after-a-death/organisations-you-need-to-contact-and-tell-us-once). It is available for people who were living in England, Scotland or Wales, not Northern Ireland. Use the reference within 28 days. Check the service's current coverage, including participating pension schemes, rather than assuming every public or workplace pension is included.

Separately notify banks, building societies, private pension providers, insurers, an employer and the landlord or mortgage provider as applicable. Ask what happens to joint accounts and essential direct debits before assuming all payments should stop. Anyone receiving their own benefits linked to the deceased person should contact their paying office separately. Keep the service confirmation and remaining private contacts in the same record.

body.heading: Two calls that reduce repeat work

items.line: The death occurred in your area. Which certification must arrive before we can register, who is eligible to register, and what date should we work to if there is a delay?
I need to report a death and understand your bereavement process. What evidence do you need, which payments or survivor benefits need checking, and will you confirm the next steps in writing?

body.heading: Documents, expenses and legal boundaries
paragraphs: Before buying multiple certified copies, list who needs one and ask whether copies are returned or digital evidence is accepted. Save funeral estimates and signed contracts. The person signing may be taking on a payment obligation; do not rely on an assumed immediate release of estate funds.

Probate, confirmation in Scotland, and estate administration are not interchangeable with simply finding your name in a will. What evidence an institution requires depends on the assets and jurisdiction. Read [the UK executor guide](/guides/named-executor-what-you-agreed-to-uk) before accepting transactions as routine. Do not divide belongings or send inheritances while debts, ownership or entitlement remain unresolved.

Seek a solicitor promptly for disputed wills, suspected abuse, foreign assets, an insolvent estate, a continuing business or pressure to distribute money. Check legal and tax deadlines early; taking longer over the house does not make every estate deadline optional.

items.q: Does the five-day registration deadline run from death?
items.a: For England and Wales, current GOV.UK guidance says to register within five days of medical-examiner confirmation that you can register. Scotland and Northern Ireland have different processes. Record which national route applies and ask the relevant registrar about a referral, missing certification or a deadline you cannot meet.

items.q: Can I contact a funeral director before registration?
items.a: Yes, you can discuss arrangements while the required paperwork is pending. Do not confuse that conversation with authorization for a burial or cremation to take place. Ask the funeral director and registrar which documents are needed and whether any proposed date must remain provisional.

items.q: Does Tell Us Once close my parent's bank accounts?
items.a: No. You still need to contact banks and other private organizations through their bereavement routes. Tell Us Once covers relevant government bodies and participating schemes, not every financial provider. Keep a separate list of private contacts and check the effect on joint accounts and household payments before requesting changes.

what-to-do-when-a-parent-dies-uk.seoTitle: What to do when a parent dies (UK)

what-to-do-when-a-parent-dies.title: What to do when a parent dies: first steps (US)
what-to-do-when-a-parent-dies.dek: Handle the first calls, protect anyone relying on your parent, and separate urgent paperwork from estate decisions that need legal authority.
what-to-do-when-a-parent-dies.metaDescription: Handle the first calls, protect anyone relying on your parent, and separate urgent paperwork from estate decisions that need legal authority.

paragraphs: When a parent dies in the US, first follow the hospital, hospice or emergency-service instructions for confirming the death. Then check anyone dependent on them, secure immediate property risks, choose funeral arrangements and find out who may handle the estate. You do not need to settle everything in the first two weeks.

You may be making these calls from a hospital corridor with only your phone and a bag of belongings. Start a single dated note. Put names, reference numbers and the next promised action there, even if the rest of the paperwork remains unsorted. This guide covers administration, not legal advice or the medical determination of death.

body.heading: The first safety and contact check
items: In a hospital or care facility, ask staff who handles the next paperwork and release arrangements. For an expected hospice death at home, follow the hospice plan and call its designated number. If the death is unexpected or you are unsure whether the person has died, call 911 and follow instructions.
Check whether a surviving partner, child or other dependent needs someone present, food, medicines or transport. Arrange pet care and a responsible contact for the next night.
Check that the home can be secured. Report an urgent leak, heating failure or other immediate hazard through the appropriate service; do not begin clearing possessions.
Ask about an existing funeral plan and the person authorized to make arrangements. Keep that decision separate from deciding who administers the estate.
Find the original will or contact the lawyer who may hold it. Promptly ask the relevant probate court about depositing a will, deadlines and appointment requirements.

paragraphs: [Open the free first-two-weeks bereavement call record](/guides/print/library/what-to-do-when-a-parent-dies.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: Four steps separate confirmation of death, immediate care, paperwork and estate authority.
body.caption: A safety check comes before sorting an estate.

body.heading: Funeral decisions and certificate copies
paragraphs: Ask funeral homes for itemized prices before accepting a package. The FTC explains that you can buy services separately. Ask who will sign the contract and who is expected to pay it; a hope of reimbursement from the estate is not the same as having money available now. Write down the agreed total and any later charges.

Death-certificate copies are not a bulk-buying test. Make a list of institutions, then ask whether each needs a certified copy, returns it, or accepts a photocopy. The issuing route is normally the vital records office in the state where the death occurred. Your funeral director can explain local ordering arrangements. [USAGov explains certificate requests](https://www.usa.gov/death-certificate).

body.heading: A first-two-weeks contact record
rows: Has the death been reported to Social Security?
What changes if the property is unoccupied?
Written instructions and any inspection requirements
What documents and authority does this account require?
Document checklist, not an assumed closure date
Must a will be deposited now, and who can apply?
Current local instructions and filing dates

body.heading: A will nominates; it does not answer every authority question
paragraphs: Being named executor does not automatically let you withdraw money or sell property. Court appointment or a state-specific alternative may be necessary. Joint ownership, beneficiary designations and trusts can follow different procedures. Arranging the funeral also does not confer estate authority. Ask the institution what it requires rather than testing the deceased person's login.

Keep estate money separate from your own and record any necessary expense you pay. Before agreeing to pay a collector personally, get advice about your responsibility. The [FTC describes debts after a death](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/debts-and-deceased-relatives): the estate generally owes them, but co-signing, some spousal obligations and mishandling estate duties can change the position.

body.alt: A bereavement call record tracks the institution, required evidence and next follow-up date.
body.caption: Notify, establish requirements, then let the authorized person take the next action.

body.heading: Social Security: identify the payment period
paragraphs: Confirm whether the funeral home reported the death; [SSA explains how to report it](https://www.ssa.gov/personal-record/when-someone-dies) if it did not. Do not spend a questionable deposit while checking it. A payment arriving during the month of death is not necessarily a payment for that month. Retirement benefits generally relate to the preceding month; other benefit programs can differ. Ask SSA and the bank to identify the payment period and required return process rather than sending a guessed amount.

Invented example: a parent dies in October and a deposit arrives around that time. The child writes down its date, amount and payment description, then asks which benefit month it covers. That question is more useful than assuming every October deposit must be returned. The institution, not this example, determines the result.

body.heading: A useful first call

items.line: My parent has died. I am gathering the requirements, not asking to transfer money today. Which team handles this, what documents do you need, and does anyone need to act before a particular date?
Please find the insurer contact and check whether the house needs an unoccupied-property notification. Write down what they say; do not cancel the policy.

body.heading: What can wait, and what needs help
paragraphs: Sorting clothing, dividing keepsakes and closing every subscription can usually follow the safety and authority checks. Preserve phones, mail and relevant records while the authorized person establishes the lawful access route. Do not use a remembered password as permission. Use [the account-search guide](/guides/how-to-find-someones-accounts-after-they-die) when you are ready to trace institutions.

Seek an estate attorney promptly if relatives disagree, there is suspected theft, the estate may owe more than it owns, a business needs decisions, or property spans jurisdictions. Ask about tax and creditor deadlines early even when the full estate work will take longer. A court clerk can explain forms and procedure but cannot choose a legal strategy for you.

items.q: How many death certificates should I order?
items.a: There is no universal number. List the banks, insurers, pension providers and other organizations likely to need evidence, then ask which require certified copies and whether they return them. Keep track of outstanding copies so you do not repeatedly order documents that could be reused.

items.q: Can I leave the house alone for two weeks?
items.a: Not without checking the circumstances. Dependants, pets, security, leaks, weather exposure and insurance conditions may need attention immediately. That does not mean you need to clear or sell the house. Arrange a named person to check it and ask the insurer what the policy requires.

items.q: Do I have to pay my parent's debts?
items.a: Not simply because you are their child. Debts are generally handled through the estate, but joint obligations, co-signing and some state-specific responsibilities can matter. Do not promise personal payment to end an upsetting call. Save the demand and ask an estate attorney about your actual position.

what-to-record-when-you-buy-an-appliance.title: What to record when you buy an appliance
what-to-record-when-you-buy-an-appliance.dek: Keep the exact model, serial number, purchase and installation evidence, warranty terms and service details in one usable appliance record.
what-to-record-when-you-buy-an-appliance.metaDescription: Keep the exact model, serial number, purchase and installation evidence, warranty terms and service details in one usable appliance record.

paragraphs: When you buy an appliance, record its exact model and serial number, seller and purchase evidence, installation date, written warranty terms and the location of its manual. Photograph the identification label safely and type the identifiers into a searchable note. Do not guess a warranty end date from the brand alone.

Delivery day can leave you with packaging in the hallway and a receipt buried in email. You do not have to build a whole home inventory now. Make one record for the new item while you can still connect the paperwork to the actual machine. This guide concerns records, not installation or repair instructions.

body.heading: Capture the details that are difficult to recover later
items: Name the appliance and location so another person can distinguish it from similar units. Copy the exact model including suffixes, not only the marketing name.
Photograph the serial label where safely accessible, then transcribe it carefully and check letters against digits. Do not move heavy equipment or remove service covers just for a photo.
Save the receipt or invoice, seller, order reference, purchase date and price. Keep delivery and installation evidence separately if those dates differ.
Save the written warranty and identify who provides it, when coverage starts, what is covered and how claims are made. Mark uncertain dates for confirmation.
Keep the correct owner manual and any installer documentation, commissioning record or required certificate. Link files to this appliance rather than leaving them in a general downloads folder.
Record any model-specific consumable or accessory specification you actually need, such as the approved filter part number. Verify it in the correct manual before buying spares.
Check the official recall information for the exact affected model or serial range and follow any applicable safety instruction.

paragraphs: [Open the free new appliance evidence record](/guides/print/library/what-to-record-when-you-buy-an-appliance.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: An appliance record connects exact identity, purchase and installation evidence, warranty and care documents.
body.caption: A searchable identifier and its evidence should stay together.

body.heading: Model and serial answer different questions
paragraphs: The model identifies a product configuration; the serial identifies the particular unit. Repair, warranty or recall enquiries can need both. [GE's official locator](https://www.geappliances.com/ge/find-model-serial-number/) provides product-specific help finding them. Locations differ, so do not assume every refrigerator or washer uses the same label position.

A photograph is useful only if it is readable. Check focus and glare before closing the door or discarding packaging. A photo can preserve a transcription error just as easily as a typed note if you capture the wrong sticker. Keep the full label and the text together, without posting serial details publicly.

body.heading: Invented example: a new dishwasher record
rows: Exact model and serial copied from the door-edge label; readable photo saved.
Seller invoice and installer handover stored with the item.
Written terms saved; coverage start and labor terms still being confirmed.
Ask the provider which date controls coverage, then record its answer.

body.alt: Three checks distinguish included warranty, paid service contract and official recall applicability.
body.caption: An expired warranty does not answer whether a safety notice applies.

body.heading: Keep the terms, not just a single expiry date
paragraphs: A warranty may distinguish parts, labor, certain components, shipping and different coverage periods. A paid service contract is also not necessarily the same thing as the included warranty. The [FTC warranty guide](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/warranties) explains why the written conditions and claims route matter. This page does not decide whether an extra plan is worth buying.

Check registration instructions in the actual terms and applicable law. Do not assume either that registration always creates coverage or that it never affects an additional benefit. Save any registration confirmation, but do not confuse it with proof of purchase or a guarantee that every future fault will be covered.

body.heading: Recall checks are independent of warranty dates
paragraphs: Use the [CPSC recall and safety-warning listings](https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls) in the US and compare the identifiers specified in any relevant notice. A similar appearance is not enough to establish a match. A recall remedy can have its own process; follow the exact notice rather than applying a general repair idea.

Registration or official alerts can help you hear about later notices, but a general alert is not a substitute for checking whether your unit falls in an affected range. If a notice says to stop use, do not wait for the next maintenance reminder or assume an expired warranty makes the notice irrelevant.

body.heading: If the appliance came with the house
paragraphs: Record purchase date and warranty status as unknown unless you have evidence. Ask the previous owner, installer or manufacturer what can be recovered. Do not assign an invented age from its appearance or promise transferable warranty coverage. Use [the model-number guide](/guides/how-to-find-the-model-number-on-any-appliance) for identification before contacting support.

After any repair, add the date, fault reported, work completed, provider and evidence. When an item is sold, removed or replaced, mark that change so a future owner does not order parts for the old machine. Share useful manuals and records while removing payment details and other personal information that do not belong in the handover.

items.q: Is a receipt enough for an appliance record?
items.a: It proves some purchase details but may not identify the exact installed unit or explain coverage conditions. Keep it with the model, serial, installation evidence and written warranty. That combination lets you answer a support enquiry without trying to reconstruct which machine an old invoice described.

items.q: Should I write one warranty end date?
items.a: Only when the written terms support that date and scope. Some coverage periods differ by component or parts versus labor, and start dates can depend on the terms. Record the document and any uncertainty. A clear pending question is better than a confident but invented expiry date.

items.q: What if I cannot reach the identification label safely?
items.a: Do not pull out a heavy or connected appliance, climb onto it or remove service covers just to finish the record. Check the manual, packaging, delivery paperwork or manufacturer locator first. Ask an installer or technician to capture the label during appropriate safe access if necessary.

where-to-look-for-a-will.title: How to find a will after someone dies (US)
where-to-look-for-a-will.dek: Search likely custodians, preserve every version and ask the right court about depositing an original, without assuming a found will gives you authority.
where-to-look-for-a-will.metaDescription: Search likely custodians, preserve every version and ask the right court about depositing an original, without assuming a found will gives you authority.

paragraphs: To find a will after someone dies in the US, check the person's lawful paper storage, ask the drafting attorney or successor firm, and contact the probate court serving their last residence. Ask about a safe-deposit box through the bank's deceased-customer process. Keep a search record, preserve every version and check local deposit requirements promptly.

You may have heard only that the will is with a lawyer, without knowing which lawyer or whether the document at home is the signed original. Treat that as a lead rather than an answer. This guide concerns finding and preserving evidence; it cannot determine whether a document is valid or which state's law governs a disputed estate.

body.heading: Search without changing the evidence
items: Ask the person coordinating the estate whether an original, copy, later amendment or attorney contact is already known. Agree who will record the search.
Check accessible files, document boxes and other places you are entitled to search. Keep papers together and note where each document was found.
Contact the drafting attorney or firm through independently verified details. Ask whether it holds an original, only a copy, or a record of transfer to another custodian.
If a lawyer retired or a firm closed, ask about the successor practice or file custodian. A local bar association may help identify the correct enquiry route.
Ask the probate clerk whether a will or estate case has already been lodged, and whether local law provides for depositing wills before death. No result is not proof that no will exists.
If a bank box or locked storage is involved, ask for the specific lawful access procedure. Do not assume possession of a key grants access to the contents.
Photograph or copy found documents for reference while preserving originals intact. Record custody and ask the court about the required next step.

paragraphs: [Open the free will search and custody record](/guides/print/library/where-to-look-for-a-will.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: A will-search sequence covers papers, professional custodians, court enquiries and preservation of all versions.
body.caption: A search and a will-deposit deadline may need to proceed at the same time.

body.heading: Ask about the deadline early, not after the whole search
paragraphs: Finding every possible version can take time, but a custodian's duty to deposit an original may already have started. [Florida section 732.901](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0700-0799/0732/Sections/0732.901.html) requires the custodian to deposit the will with the court having venue within ten days after receiving information of the death. That is a Florida example, not a national deadline.

California court guidance describes a different deadline: thirty days after learning of the death for delivering the original, subject to the applicable rules. Ask the relevant clerk for current instructions, required accompanying information and whether there are related copy-delivery duties. Depositing a will and applying to administer an estate are separate acts. Do not postpone the first because you are not ready for the second.

body.heading: Record what you found, not what you assume
rows: A lawyer or proposed plan existed.
Whether any valid version was later executed.
A copy of a signed document
A version and possible custodian can be identified.
Where the original is and whether it was changed or revoked.
An original document has been located.
Validity, later amendments and applicable deposit or probate requirements.
A document or proceeding was filed there.
Its status, completeness and effect on the present estate.

body.heading: Invented example: a copy and a later document
paragraphs: A niece finds a photocopy dated several years earlier. The firm named on it says the original was returned to the client. She records that answer and asks the bank about lawful access to a box mentioned in correspondence. A later signed document is eventually found through the permitted process.

She keeps both versions, the firm's response and the discovery dates. She does not destroy the earlier copy or decide that a later date alone proves the newer paper governs. A probate attorney reviews the documents, including whether an amendment changes only part of an earlier will. The example is about evidence handling, not a rule for choosing between wills.

body.alt: A comparison distinguishes what a draft, copy and original will can establish and what remains uncertain.
body.caption: A date and signature appearance do not resolve a contested validity question.

body.heading: A will does not appoint you by discovery
paragraphs: Read who is nominated, but do not assume that person can immediately withdraw money or sell property. [New York Courts explains fiduciary appointment](https://www.nycourts.gov/help/when-someone-dies/fiduciary-estate): appointment and duties are handled through the court process there. Your state may have a different procedure or a small-estate alternative. Finding the will does not make the finder the representative.

Do not use a deceased person's login or power-of-attorney paperwork as a shortcut to search private accounts. Ask the institution and an estate adviser what access is permitted after death. Beneficiary designations, jointly owned property and trusts may follow routes outside the will, so the will itself is not necessarily an inventory of everything the person owned.

body.heading: Make the enquiry specific

items.line: I am trying to locate the original will for [name], who died on [date]. Please tell me your verification requirements, whether you hold a document, and whether your records identify another custodian.
I have located a document described as a will. Which court has the deposit process, what deadline applies to the custodian, and how should the original and any amendments be delivered?

body.heading: If no original appears, or relatives disagree
paragraphs: Keep the search log and seek advice about the next process. A missing original does not automatically mean there was never a will, and a photocopy is not automatically useless. Local evidence rules determine what can be proved. Similarly, do not assume an informal handwritten note is either valid or invalid without advice.

Escalate promptly if someone refuses to produce a known document, pages appear missing or altered, property is being distributed, or there are competing claims about capacity or pressure. Do not confront a disputed document by writing on it or destroying another version. Preserve what you have and ask about protective steps.

If the estate proceeds without a valid will, the applicable intestacy and appointment rules determine the route. They are not a family vote about what seems fair. Use [the US executor guide](/guides/named-executor-what-you-agreed-to) to understand the distinction between locating documents and accepting estate administration.

items.q: Can I search for the will online?
items.a: You can check the relevant court's official records and any locally available deposit or registry process, but no universal US website contains every private will. A negative search does not prove absence. Combine court enquiries with the home-paperwork and attorney-custodian search, keeping dates and responses.

items.q: Does the newest document always win?
items.a: Not simply because its date is later. Validity, amendments, revocation and the interaction between documents can matter. Preserve all versions and ask a qualified estate attorney to assess them. Do not tear up an older will or mark it cancelled based only on your own reading.

items.q: Can I open a bank box if I have its key?
items.a: A key is not a universal authorization. The bank and applicable state law determine who can access a deceased customer's box, what evidence is required and what may be removed. Ask specifically about a will-search procedure and keep any bank record of the access and document handling.

appliance-warranties-what-to-track.title: Appliance warranty tracking: dates, terms and claims
appliance-warranties-what-to-track.dek: Keep the receipt, model and serial, coverage details and claim route together, then check what is covered before authorizing a repair.
appliance-warranties-what-to-track.metaDescription: Keep the receipt, model and serial, coverage details and claim route together, then check what is covered before authorizing a repair.

paragraphs: Track the appliance's identity, proof of purchase, warranty start rule, separate coverage periods and claim instructions. Keep the actual warranty terms, not just an expiry reminder. Before authorizing a paid repair, ask what the warranty covers and whether the provider requires a particular claim process.

A label saying 'ten-year warranty' can hide different periods for a major component, other parts and labor. A single calendar date may therefore give the wrong impression. This guide concerns ordinary US appliance warranty administration, not a review of paid home-service plans.

body.heading: Build one warranty record
items: Photograph the full rating plate and record the exact model and serial.
Save the receipt, order confirmation, delivery and installation evidence available.
Download the warranty version applying to the purchase rather than relying on a current marketing page.
Record what event starts each coverage period.
Separate component, parts and labor periods and any stated limits.
Note registration status, transfer rules and documented maintenance requirements actually found in the terms.
Save the official claims contact and authorization procedure.
Keep service visits and claim correspondence attached to the appliance record.

paragraphs: [Open the free appliance coverage and claim record](/guides/print/library/appliance-warranties-what-to-track.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: Four warranty checks distinguish start rule, parts, labor and claim process.
body.caption: The largest advertised number may not describe the whole repair.

body.heading: Write terms you can trace back
paragraphs: For each summary, record the page or heading in the warranty. 'Coverage starts from installation under section 2' is checkable; 'installed sometime last spring, probably covered' is not. If the terms are unclear, ask the manufacturer or seller and retain the response.

The [FTC](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/warranties) advises keeping the warranty and receipt and checking coverage and claims procedures. This record cannot decide whether a particular failure is a covered defect. Do not write that most claims fail because of paperwork; that would need evidence this guide does not have.

body.heading: Invented example: separate coverage questions
rows: Which purchase or installation event controls?
What component is named, and for how long?
Are there separate terms or limits?
Who pays and under what authorization?
What documented care does this product require?
Who approves work and what evidence is needed?

body.heading: A warranty and a service contract differ
paragraphs: A manufacturer's warranty and a separately purchased service contract can have different providers, exclusions, fees and claims routes. 'Extended warranty' is often used loosely. Read the actual agreement before treating it as an extension of the original manufacturer's obligations.

Do not assume a whole-home plan covers every appliance, renews on the same terms or pays every visit fee. Keep the contract's own record if you have one. This guide does not recommend buying a plan or predict whether its price will be worthwhile.

body.alt: Four stages track an appliance fault through contact, authorization and retained evidence.
body.caption: Submitting a claim does not establish that the repair is approved.

body.heading: Do not invent a maintenance condition
paragraphs: Some terms connect coverage to proper use and maintenance, but there is no universal annual-service rule covering all furnaces, water heaters and appliances. Copy the condition actually applicable to your model. Keep maintenance evidence without inventing a visit that did not happen.

Nor should you assume that using an independent repairer voids the entire warranty. FTC guidance explains restrictions on requirements to use specified parts or services. Damage caused by improper work and an unlawful blanket restriction are different questions. Ask for a written explanation of a refusal and seek qualified consumer advice if needed.

body.heading: Before authorizing a repair

items.line: My appliance has this model and serial, and I have these purchase documents. Which parts of this fault may be covered?
Do I need a claim number or approval before anyone starts work, and what costs could remain mine?
Please identify the term or reason for the coverage decision and the review process in writing.

body.heading: Track the claim separately from the expiry
paragraphs: Record when the fault was observed, when you contacted the provider, what was submitted and the promised next step. Do not assume a reminder just before expiry preserves a claim or that a submitted form means approval. Check the actual reporting requirements.

If a visit is arranged, ask who is coming, what was authorized and how additional work will be approved. Afterward, keep the service record and any changed coverage terms with the claim. Use [the repair record guide](/guides/what-to-keep-after-a-home-repair) for what to capture.

body.heading: A safety recall is another route
paragraphs: Search the [CPSC recall listings](https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls) and manufacturer guidance if there is a safety concern. Match model, serial range and other identifiers to the actual notice and follow its instructions. A broad search result for the brand does not establish that your unit is affected.

Do not wait for a warranty appointment to respond to an immediate hazard. Stop and obtain appropriate emergency or professional help for dangerous symptoms. A warranty record is administrative evidence, not permission to keep using unsafe equipment.

items.q: What if I lost the receipt?
items.a: Ask the retailer, installer or account history for available proof, and ask the warrantor what alternative evidence it accepts. A serial may identify the unit but not necessarily prove the purchase date or owner. Do not substitute an invented purchase date for missing documentation.

items.q: Does registration always extend coverage?
items.a: No. Effects vary by product, terms and applicable law. Check whether registration is requested, what benefit is offered and what evidence confirms completion. Keep the response or confirmation, but do not assume a marketing invitation creates a longer warranty.

items.q: Can the warranty transfer to a buyer?
items.a: Check the written transfer rules and any required process or deadline. Do not promise transferable coverage when selling an appliance or home based only on the original term. Record whether transfer is confirmed, restricted or unknown and direct the buyer to the actual terms.

sources.note: Written terms, receipts, service contracts and claim procedures.

sources.name: CPSC: Recalls and product safety warnings
sources.note: Official recall search and safety notices; follow the actual notice for a matching product.

beneficiary-forms-override-your-will.title: Beneficiary vs will: what controls each account?
beneficiary-forms-override-your-will.dek: Check which assets follow a beneficiary designation, which may enter your estate, and when spouse rights or conflicting paperwork need advice.
beneficiary-forms-override-your-will.metaDescription: Check which assets follow a beneficiary designation, which may enter your estate, and when spouse rights or conflicting paperwork need advice.

paragraphs: A valid beneficiary designation commonly controls the payment of an account or policy rather than the instructions in a will. But 'the form always wins' is too absolute: spouse protections, plan terms, court orders, ownership and state or federal law can change the result. Check the provider's current record and get advice about conflicts.

An old workplace plan can be easy to miss when updating a will. The will may be current while a separate designation is years out of date. This US guide helps you inventory those separate instructions. It does not decide who should inherit or resolve a disputed claim.

body.heading: Start with the way the asset is held
paragraphs: Ask whether the asset is individually owned, jointly held with a relevant survivorship provision, held in trust or subject to a beneficiary arrangement. These are different routes. An account with no beneficiary does not necessarily pass under a will: the plan's default provision may identify a recipient, and other ownership rules may apply.

The [Supreme Court of Texas will instructions](https://www.txcourts.gov/media/1456774/239037.pdf) specifically warn that a new will does not change beneficiary designations on listed assets. That is a useful example of the distinction, not permission to apply Texas rules to every household.

body.heading: Questions to ask for each asset
rows: Current designation, spouse rights and any applicable domestic relations order
Designation, custodian defaults and relevant state-law questions
Policy owner, insured person, beneficiaries and accepted changes
Whether the designation is active and what happens if it fails
Ownership documents and controlling terms, with legal advice where needed

body.heading: Audit the provider records
items: List current and former employers' retirement plans, personal retirement accounts and insurance policies.
Ask each provider for the primary and contingent beneficiaries currently accepted on file.
Check names, relationships, contact details and any shares shown, without posting private data on a shared checklist.
Ask what happens if a beneficiary has died, cannot be found or is not eligible.
Check consent, signature and submission requirements before making a change.
Submit through the official process and retain acceptance confirmation.
Record the check date and where confirmation is stored; set a review after significant life changes.

paragraphs: [Open the free beneficiary designation audit](/guides/print/library/beneficiary-forms-override-your-will.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: Four checks distinguish ownership, beneficiary designations, legal exceptions and estate assets.
body.caption: The controlling route depends on more than the date of the will.

body.heading: Invented example: a form and a will disagree
paragraphs: Morgan's will leaves the estate to two adult children. A retirement account record still names a sibling. The useful next action is not writing 'children' in a household binder. Morgan asks the administrator to confirm the designation and explain the change procedure, including any spouse-related requirement.

After submitting a new form, Morgan saves the administrator's confirmation. Until acceptance is established, the checklist says 'change submitted, awaiting confirmation,' not 'updated.' This example illustrates a recordkeeping process, not a predicted distribution.

body.alt: Three record stages show confirmation of the current form, submission and accepted change.
body.caption: A household note cannot replace the provider's change process.

body.heading: Marriage and divorce need extra care
paragraphs: The [IRS death-of-spouse guidance](https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/plan-participant-employee/retirement-topics-death-of-spouse) notes that many retirement plans require a spouse as primary beneficiary unless written consent allows an alternative. Do not assume an ordinary online edit can override that protection.

Likewise, do not assume divorce automatically removes an ex-spouse, or that it never does. Asset type, applicable law, orders and plan administration matter. Ask the administrator and a qualified attorney about your specific situation. Do not ignore a divorce order or settlement while trying to simplify a beneficiary record.

body.heading: When to stop filling in the form
paragraphs: Pause for a minor beneficiary, a person receiving means-tested benefits, a trust, blended-family disagreement, international assets or conflicting documents. These choices can have legal and tax consequences beyond the provider's form. Avoid naming another adult 'to pass it on later' without advice; that may not create the arrangement you intend.

If the account owner has died, this is no longer a routine update. Contact the provider's bereavement or claims team and the authorized estate representative. Do not use a saved login to change beneficiaries after death. Preserve forms, confirmations and correspondence for the claims process.

body.heading: Ask the administrator

items.line: Please confirm the primary and contingent beneficiaries currently accepted for this account, and the date of the latest designation.
What spouse-consent rules, court orders or plan defaults could affect this change, and where can I obtain the governing instructions?
How will I know the new designation has been accepted, rather than merely uploaded?

body.heading: Make the household note an index
paragraphs: Record the provider, account type, date checked and location of accepted documentation. Keep sensitive identifiers in a protected record rather than a broadly shared planning page. Your index helps someone find evidence; it is not itself the beneficiary designation.

Review the [if-something-happens file](/guides/the-if-something-happens-to-me-file) for the larger document index. Keep the jobs separate: a will expresses estate instructions, provider forms address particular benefits, and legal advice coordinates conflicts. None substitutes automatically for the others.

items.q: Does a newer will replace an older beneficiary form?
items.a: Usually not for an asset governed by a valid beneficiary designation, but the actual result depends on the asset and applicable rules. Ask the provider to confirm the designation and consult an attorney if there is a conflict. Updating the will alone is not a reliable account-update method.

items.q: What if the beneficiary field is blank?
items.a: Ask for the plan or policy's default order. A spouse, other person or estate may receive the benefit depending on those terms and applicable law. Do not assume either that probate is inevitable or that the will definitely controls merely because you cannot see a named beneficiary online.

items.q: Can I name a child directly?
items.a: The provider may permit it, but a minor's receipt and management of funds can require arrangements under applicable law. Children with disabilities or benefits may need additional planning. Discuss an appropriate structure with a qualified attorney rather than treating an adult relative's informal promise as a substitute.

sources.name: Supreme Court of Texas: Will form instructions
sources.note: Texas instructions distinguish beneficiary assets from assets controlled by a will.
