The app shows two numbers, and the larger one is tempting. The problem is not choosing the optimistic balance. It is working out what each number already includes, and what still has to leave the account. Subtracting every pending item again can be just as misleading as ignoring every commitment.

This guide concerns deposit-account balances, not credit-card available credit. It is general organisation guidance, not a prediction that a bank will honour a particular payment. Read your own account terms and contact the bank about unclear transactions, holds or an unexpected balance.

body.heading: Read the label before using the number

left.label: Current or posted balance
items: Often shows transactions that have posted to the account, under the bank's own definitions.
Useful for matching posted activity and statements, but not a guarantee that all committed money is free.

right.label: Available balance
items: Reflects the bank's current availability calculation, which may account for holds and pending activity.
Still needs checking against unposted commitments and the account terms; do not treat it as a guaranteed safe-to-spend amount.

body.heading: Check the balance without double-counting
items: Note which account and balance label you are using, and the time you checked it.
Inspect pending transactions and holds. Establish whether each is already reflected in the displayed available amount.
List outstanding commitments the bank does not yet reflect, such as a bill you still need to pay or a payment not yet presented.
Keep the money needed before your next reliable income available in the appropriate account. Do not include uncertain income as if it has arrived.
Ask the bank about anything you cannot reconcile, especially unfamiliar charges, negative balances or a hold affecting an important payment.

paragraphs: [Open the free available balance and commitments check](/guides/print/library/available-balance-vs-current-balance.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: A balance check distinguishes amounts already reflected, commitments still to cover and unclear items to verify with the bank.
body.caption: Do not count the same commitment twice.

body.heading: An invented example with one subtraction, not two
body.intro: These figures illustrate a method, not a bank's universal posting rules. Assume the pending purchase is already included in the bank's available balance.
rows: Not the chosen spending starting point in this example
Do not subtract this a second time from available
The starting figure after confirming the assumption
Upcoming bill not reflected by the bank
$920 minus $250, before any other commitments or buffer

body.heading: A pending item is not a promise about the final result
paragraphs: A pending amount may change, be replaced by a final transaction or disappear from the immediate view. That alone does not tell you that an obligation has been cancelled. Ask the merchant or bank about the relevant transaction rather than relying on its temporary appearance.

In its [posting guidance](https://www.chase.com/personal/checking/overdraft-services/how-transactions-post), Chase says that pending activity affects available balance, that some authorised transactions may not appear as pending, and that daytime display does not guarantee later payment. This is a specific bank's explanation, not a rule copied across every provider.

If your bank includes an overdraft facility or another credit arrangement in what it displays, separate borrowed availability from your own funds. Check the terms, costs and payment consequences. Do not count a lending limit as income or assume that every account displays it in the same way.

body.alt: A worked balance example subtracts a 250-dollar unreflected bill from 920 dollars available without deducting a pending purchase twice.
body.caption: An invented example, not a payment guarantee or a universal bank calculation.

body.heading: The bank cannot reserve an intention it has not received
paragraphs: A bill due next week, a cheque not yet presented, or groceries still to buy may not be represented in the number on screen. Your record supplies that missing context. Keep a [monthly bills list](/guides/monthly-bills-list) and review [what is due before direct debits leave](/guides/what-to-check-before-each-direct-debit-date).

An invented example: the app shows enough for an optional purchase, but an annual insurance payment is due before payday and has not reached the bank. The account is not wrong. The spending decision is missing a commitment. For that broader decision, use [how much money is actually safe to spend](/guides/how-much-of-your-money-is-actually-safe-to-spend).

The opposite mistake is reserving the same purchase in three places: it reduced available, it remains in a pending list, and it is also included in an upcoming-bills total. Match individual items before subtracting totals. A more conservative number is not automatically a more accurate one.

body.heading: Ask the bank a question it can answer

items.line: Which transactions or holds are included in my available balance, and what does the current balance mean on this account? I need to understand this specific item before relying on the displayed amount.
This payment is due and the balance display is unclear. What has posted, what is still pending, and which account terms or processing conditions should I check?

body.heading: Two balances, several possible explanations

items.q: Should I use current or available balance before spending?
items.a: Available balance is often the more relevant immediate availability figure, but check how your own bank defines it. Account separately for commitments not already reflected. Neither balance guarantees a payment will clear or tells you what is affordable after all upcoming needs. Do not automatically subtract pending items twice.

items.q: Why is my available balance lower than my current balance?
items.a: Pending transactions, deposit availability rules or holds may explain a difference, depending on your account. Open the detailed activity and ask the bank about unclear entries. Do not infer that a particular hold has expired, that a merchant was paid or that a deposit is fully usable from the difference alone.

items.q: Does money disappearing from pending mean I can spend it?
items.a: Not necessarily. A pending display can change before the final transaction arrives. Keep your own record of what you authorised and ask the bank or merchant if the status is unclear. Removing an item from a screen is not the same as confirming that the underlying obligation has ended.

body.heading: Use the account number with the rest of the picture
paragraphs: Start with a balance you understand, match the items already represented, and reserve what remains due. You are building a spending decision, not trying to make the banking app show a more reassuring number.

[Personal Finance Companion](/shop/personal-finance-companion) is an optional organiser for the financial information you enter. It cannot decide what your bank will pay or make an uncertain balance reliable. The worksheet here works without connecting a bank account or buying a product.

sources.name: Chase: how transactions post
sources.note: Bank-specific example: pending transactions affect available balance, some transactions are not visible as pending and daytime visibility does not guarantee later payment.

homeschool-record-keeping-template.title: Homeschool record keeping template you can keep using
homeschool-record-keeping-template.dek: Record the date, what was actually covered and one useful observation. Add evidence when it matters, and keep legal requirements separate.
homeschool-record-keeping-template.metaDescription: Copy a simple homeschool record keeping template with dates, lesson references, observations and evidence. Includes a free printable record sheet.

paragraphs: A usable homeschool record keeping template records the date, the subject and lesson or activity, what actually happened, and a short observation or evidence reference when useful. Keep a separate place for required attendance, assessments and legal filings. A learning log can support your records, but it does not automatically satisfy every state's rules.

The record is easy to postpone when the lesson has already taken the morning. Then a few weeks pass and you remember that there was science, but not which experiment, what changed, or where the photo went. The template's job is to leave a small trail while the details are still available.

This guide is for US homeschool parents who want a practical daily record on paper, in a spreadsheet or in a chosen app. It is not a curriculum, a grading system or a legal compliance certificate. Check the requirements for your child's actual educational route before deciding what must be kept or submitted.

body.heading: Copy these four columns
rows: Name the book, unit, lesson or activity
Record completed, partly completed or changed work
Note a useful observation or where a sample is kept
Use a reference you can find again
Do not copy a plan as if it happened
Leave this short when nothing more is needed

body.heading: Make the first entry small and specific
items: Choose one place for each child's record. Add the child's name or identifier where more than one child uses the same sheet.
After the learning activity, record the actual date and enough detail to identify the work later.
Write what happened rather than what was scheduled. Mark unfinished or changed work without turning the entry into a judgment about the child.
Add an observation or sample reference if it helps explain progress or a question to revisit.
Check separately that required attendance, subject, assessment and filing records are being maintained under the rules that apply.

paragraphs: [Open the free homeschool learning record](/guides/print/library/homeschool-record-keeping-template.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: Four learning-log fields identify the date, specific work, what actually happened and the evidence or follow-up needed.
body.caption: A completed activity is not automatically proof of understanding.

body.heading: A week of invented entries
body.intro: These examples show the level of detail, not a recommended grade-level timetable or evidence of a real child's progress.
rows: Compared halves and quarters with paper strips
Ask for an explanation without strips next time
Read together; discussed why the character left
Book title on the reading list; no additional sample needed
Stopped after the opening sentence; discussed the idea aloud
Try a spoken outline before writing
Sketch in science folder, dated Thursday

body.heading: An observation is more useful than a performance label
paragraphs: 'Difficult' tells you how the session felt, but may not explain what to do next. 'Could compare the strips but could not explain the relationship without them' names a specific question. You do not need that much detail for every activity. Save it for work where the next decision depends on what you noticed.

Likewise, 'completed' and 'understood' are not interchangeable. A child can finish a worksheet with help, explain an idea orally without producing a page, or need another approach. Use [checking whether learning stuck](/guides/how-to-check-if-your-child-learned-something) when you need a better follow-up than another tick.
Do not turn the log into continuous testing. Its purpose is to support teaching and preserve a record, not to force a score onto every conversation, book or outing.

body.alt: A three-step record, review and adjust loop turns a short learning log into a practical next teaching decision.
body.caption: Keep statutory attendance and filing obligations as a separate check.

body.heading: Keep legal requirements beside the template, not inside a guess
paragraphs: As one jurisdiction-specific example, [Florida's home-education statute](https://wwwo.leg.state.fl.us/Statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=1000-1099%2F1002%2FSections%2F1002.41.html%2F) describes an activity log made as instruction happens, reading-material titles and samples of the student's work. That example does not tell a parent in another state what their records must contain.

Find your current official rules and record the required items, deadlines and retention arrangements separately. Our [requirements verification guide](/guides/homeschool-record-keeping-requirements-by-state) explains that process. If an evaluator, school or authority requests records, confirm what is required rather than sending every private family note by default.

body.heading: Use the record for the next teaching decision

items.line: We completed this activity with help. Before moving on, I want to check whether the idea makes sense without the same prompt. I will note what happens, not assume the tick settled it.
Here is the dated log and the samples it refers to. Which additional records are required for this review, and where can I find that requirement in the current guidance?

body.heading: When the record falls behind
items: Restart with today's actual work. Do not leave a growing blank period because the earlier pages are incomplete.
Reconstruct older entries from dated work, reading lists and other evidence where possible, marking uncertain dates honestly.
Do not backfill a weekly plan as a completed attendance or learning record. Keep the difference visible.
Use [catching up on homeschool records](/guides/how-to-catch-up-on-homeschool-records) for a larger gap, and ask the relevant authority or adviser promptly if a required deadline is involved.

body.heading: Keep the template workable

items.q: Do I need an entry for every minute of homeschooling?
items.a: Not as a universal rule. This template is a learning log, not a national attendance requirement. Keep any hours, days, subjects or other evidence required for your situation separately and accurately. The useful level of detail is enough to identify actual work and support the next teaching or record-keeping decision.

items.q: Can I use the same activity entry for two children?
items.a: You can record a shared activity once for logistics, but keep each child's involvement and evidence identifiable where needed. Children may do different work or understand different parts of the same topic. Do not automatically copy the same result to everyone just because they sat at the same table.

items.q: Should I scan every worksheet into the log?
items.a: Not automatically. Keep the material your applicable rules require and useful samples that explain the work. A dated reference to where a sample is stored may be more manageable than attaching everything. Check submission and retention requirements before discarding originals or assuming a digital copy is sufficient.

body.heading: A record you will open tomorrow
paragraphs: Use the smallest record that preserves the information you actually need. For selecting evidence across a year, read [what goes in a homeschool portfolio](/guides/what-goes-in-a-homeschool-portfolio). The log and portfolio serve related but different purposes.

If keeping separate subjects and records for several children is the difficult part, [Homeschooling Companion](/shop/homeschooling-companion) is an optional organiser, not a curriculum or a compliance guarantee. The free record sheet here works on its own.

sources.name: Florida Legislature: home education programmes, section 1002.41
sources.note: Official statutory example of a contemporaneous activity log, reading-material titles and work samples. Not a national record-keeping standard.

hotel-cannot-find-your-reservation.title: Hotel cannot find your reservation: what to do now
hotel-cannot-find-your-reservation.dek: Check the property, dates, guest name and booking references. If you booked through a third party, get them involved before paying twice.
hotel-cannot-find-your-reservation.metaDescription: Hotel cannot find your booking? Check names and confirmation numbers, contact the booking site, and document tonight's options before paying twice.

paragraphs: If the hotel cannot find your reservation, first confirm the exact property, arrival date, lead guest name and both the booking-site reference and hotel confirmation number. Show the original confirmation. If it was booked through a third party, contact that provider through its verified support route while asking the desk what can be established locally.

You are at the counter, the bags are heavy, and your phone says confirmed while the desk says nothing is there. The immediate job is to find out whether the booking can be located and where you can stay tonight. You do not need to settle every refund question before taking the next useful step.

This is a practical troubleshooting guide, not a guarantee of a room, compensation or a refund. Policies and legal rights depend on the booking, provider and jurisdiction. Keep the evidence and check the terms rather than accepting a generic promise from this article.

body.heading: Check the details that can actually change the search
items: Match the full property name and street address. A chain name alone is not enough, especially near airports or in cities with several branches.
Check arrival and departure dates, including a booking made for the night before a very early arrival. Ask whether the reservation was marked as a no-show or cancelled.
Read the lead guest name exactly as shown on the confirmation, including another person's surname or the person who made the booking.
Distinguish the travel site's order reference from a hotel confirmation number. Ask the desk which reference its system can search.
Check whether the message confirms accommodation or only an enquiry, payment attempt or request. Look for changes and cancellation messages as well as the first email.

paragraphs: [Open the free missing hotel reservation case sheet](/guides/print/library/hotel-cannot-find-your-reservation.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: A booking search separates the property address, dates and status, lead guest name, and provider references.
body.caption: Each detail gives the responsible provider another way to search.

body.heading: The same stay can have different references
rows: The property or brand reservation team
Can you search this reference for these dates and the lead guest name?
The provider you used to book
Can you supply the hotel's reference and confirm that the booking was transmitted?
The relevant payment provider or merchant
Is this a completed charge, a pending hold or something else?
The sender and the original booking provider
Which version of the reservation is current, and what happened to the original?

body.heading: If the hotel cannot find a third-party booking
paragraphs: Contact the company you booked with using its app, original confirmation or verified website. Do not use an unverified support number supplied in a random search result or message. Ask the provider to contact the property, verify the booking status and give you the hotel-side confirmation reference.

For a concrete policy example, [Hilton directs third-party customers](https://www.hilton.com/en-gb/help-center/reservations/can-i-book-through-a-third-party-site/) back to that provider for confirmation, changes and cancellation. Another brand or contract may work differently. The useful principle is to identify which party controls your booking, not assume the front desk can change a travel site's order.

Ask for a case reference, the person's name or department and the next promised action. If possible, ask support to speak with the property directly while you remain available. A screenshot of a confirmation is helpful evidence, but it is not proof that the desk can create a room or override inventory.

body.heading: Use the counter conversation to move the problem forward

items.line: My confirmation is for this property and these dates, under this guest name. I also have a booking-site reference. Which hotel confirmation number or other detail would help you search?
I am at the property and the desk cannot locate the stay. Can you confirm its current status, supply the hotel's reference and contact the property directly? Please give me a case reference.
What options can you confirm for tonight, and what costs or conditions apply? Please put any cancellation, replacement or reimbursement arrangement in writing before I rely on it.

body.alt: Three next steps cover booking-provider escalation, practical overnight options and a written record of agreements.
body.caption: Do not assume a replacement cost has been approved without confirmation.

body.heading: Before you pay for another room
paragraphs: If you need somewhere safe to stay, practical constraints may require a new booking. Before paying where possible, ask the original provider what it is authorising and what remains unresolved. A verbal promise that someone will sort it out later is not the same as a written commitment to cover a particular cost.

Check the new room's full price, taxes, deposit and cancellation terms. Keep the original reservation evidence and the new receipt. Do not assume a pending card hold is a second completed charge, or that a charge disappearing means a booking is valid. Your issuer can explain the transaction status and any dispute process or deadline that applies.

If you are travelling with children, have access needs, or are arriving late with limited transport, tell the desk and provider what makes a proposed alternative unsuitable. This is information they need to assess an option; it does not create a universal entitlement to a specific replacement.

body.heading: A booking that was there under another name
paragraphs: An invented example: Alex arrives with a confirmation for the right property, but the desk's first search uses Alex's surname. The lead guest on the booking is Alex's partner. Searching the lead guest name and hotel reference finds it. That is one possible cause, not a reason to blame the traveller or assume every missing booking is a spelling problem.

In a different case the provider cannot establish the booking and the hotel is full. The useful record then becomes the provider's case number, the property's confirmation of what it found, the agreed next step and any replacement costs. Keep the two situations distinct: locating a valid stay and negotiating an unresolved booking are different jobs.

body.heading: When the confirmation is not enough

items.q: Does a confirmation email guarantee that the hotel has a room for me?
items.a: It is important evidence of what was booked, but it does not resolve every issue with dates, cancellation, transmission or available inventory. Compare the exact property, guest and dates, then ask the responsible provider to confirm current status. Keep the email while the parties investigate rather than treating it as a complete answer.

items.q: Should I cancel the original reservation myself?
items.a: Not automatically. Ask the provider what cancellation would do to the existing case and any refund or replacement arrangements. If you choose to cancel, save the terms, confirmation and reason. Do not assume that cancelling a booking you cannot locate is required or harmless in every contract.

items.q: Can the front desk refund a booking made on another website?
items.a: It depends on who collected the money and the booking terms. The property may not control the travel site's payment or order. Ask both parties who can make the change and request written next steps. A brand-specific support policy is not a universal rule for every booking platform.

body.heading: Give the next conversation a starting point
paragraphs: Once tonight is sorted, keep the case trail together. Our [one-page itinerary guide](/guides/how-to-write-a-one-page-trip-itinerary) helps put each stay's address, dates and references within reach. For a disrupted connection, use the separate [flight-delay guide](/guides/flight-delayed-with-a-connection-what-to-do-first).

[Travel Companion](/shop/travel-companion) is an optional place for the travel details you enter. It does not locate a missing booking, contact a hotel or guarantee a refund. The free worksheet here can carry the same practical references without a purchase.

sources.name: Hilton Help Centre: third-party reservations
sources.note: Hilton directs guests to the original third party to confirm, modify or cancel such reservations. This is a brand-specific example, not a universal hotel policy.

the-if-something-happens-to-me-file.title: The if-something-happens-to-me file: where to start
the-if-something-happens-to-me-file.dek: Give someone a way to find the right people, papers and household details without putting every secret in one folder. Start with one useful page.
the-if-something-happens-to-me-file.metaDescription: Build an if-something-happens-to-me file with document locations, trusted contacts and household instructions. Keep access separate from authority.

paragraphs: An if-something-happens-to-me file is a map of important people, documents, accounts and household responsibilities. It tells an appropriate person what exists, where to look and whom to call. It does not give that person legal authority, change who inherits, or replace a will, power of attorney or health-care directive.

The question is smaller than sorting your entire life: if you could not explain things tomorrow, where would someone start? Not every account number. Not every password. Just enough accurate directions to stop the first person helping you from searching every drawer.

This guide is for adults preparing practical information for illness, incapacity or death. Legal authority, privacy and document requirements depend on the situation and location. Ask a qualified professional about the documents you need rather than treating this folder as a legal plan.

body.heading: Make a useful first page
items: Choose who should know that the file exists, and ask whether they are willing to help. Do not assume a relative can or wants to take on every task.
Write the location of your current legal documents and the professional or office to contact. Identify originals separately from copies.
List immediate responsibilities: dependent care, pets, essential household services, keys and any safety or access information that cannot wait.
Add the institutions where accounts and policies exist, using enough detail to identify them without exposing unnecessary credentials.
Date the page, choose a protected storage location and explain how the appropriate person can find it when needed.

paragraphs: [Open the free if-something-happens-to-me file map](/guides/print/library/the-if-something-happens-to-me-file.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: Three questions distinguish identifying information, locating it and establishing who is authorised to act.
body.caption: Finding information does not establish authority to use it.

body.heading: What belongs in the file, and what belongs elsewhere
rows: Who to contact and what role they have agreed to
Document type, location of the original and relevant professional
The originals, stored according to professional guidance
Institution, policy type and contact route
Passwords, recovery codes and full identity details
Essential contacts, responsibilities and where instructions are kept
Keys, access codes and other security information
Which account or provider has an approved legacy or recovery process
A plain-text master list of credentials accessible to everyone

body.heading: Finding a document is not the same as being allowed to act
paragraphs: Someone may know where an account is without being authorised to use it. A person named in a will may still need to follow the appropriate estate process. A person who helps with bills while you are well may not have the authority required if you lose capacity. Keep these questions separate from the practical question of where the paperwork lives.

For health-care preferences, [CaringInfo's state and territory resources](https://www.caringinfo.org/planning/advance-directives/) provide a starting point for the relevant advance-directive forms. Read the instructions for your location. An informal note about your wishes may help a conversation, but do not label it a legally effective directive without checking the requirements.

Use the [emergency contact and medical decision-maker guide](/guides/emergency-contact-and-medical-decision-maker) to distinguish being reachable from being authorised. If family circumstances, property ownership or legal arrangements are complicated, get professional advice before promising someone a role.

body.heading: A first version that is small enough to finish
paragraphs: An invented example: Maya writes that the originals of her legal documents are with a named professional, the household folder is in the locked cabinet, and her sister knows the agreed access process. She lists the mortgage provider and insurer by name, not their passwords. She adds the contact for the person who can collect her child under the school's current arrangements.

That is not a complete estate or emergency plan. It is a starting point someone can follow. The next pass adds other institutions and responsibilities. The file distinguishes an agreed role from a person Maya still needs to ask, and it dates every section so a helper can spot older information.

body.alt: A three-pass file-building process starts with urgent needs, adds document locations and checks protected access.
body.caption: Mark gaps as gaps instead of guessing.

body.heading: Have the conversation before the folder is needed

items.line: I am making a short record of where important things are. Would you be willing to know where it is and who to contact? That does not mean you are agreeing to manage everything.
I have listed where the documents are, but I want to check who may act and when. Which documents and access arrangements are appropriate for this situation?

body.heading: Check the file after a meaningful change
items: Update contact details and document locations after a move, relationship change, new dependent or changed professional adviser.
Replace superseded directions clearly rather than leaving conflicting versions in several folders.
Review access after changing a lock, device, provider or security arrangement. Do not solve access by distributing credentials indiscriminately.
Ask the appropriate person whether the directions are understandable. They should be able to locate a named document without you giving a second set of instructions.

body.heading: Before you share the file

items.q: Is an if-something-happens-to-me file the same as a will?
items.a: No. It is an information and location record. A will and other legal arrangements serve different purposes and must meet applicable requirements. Keep the location of current documents in the file, but get professional advice about their legal effect and who has authority to act.

items.q: Should I put every password in the folder?
items.a: Not as an openly accessible list. Record where approved access or recovery arrangements are managed, and protect credentials according to the relevant provider and security guidance. The appropriate process may differ during incapacity and after death. Knowing that an account exists does not authorise someone to sign in.

items.q: Is a half-finished file worth keeping?
items.a: Yes, if it clearly says what is current, what is incomplete and where the information came from. Start with immediate responsibilities and key document locations. Do not present an unfinished list as a complete legal or financial inventory, and avoid leaving a confident-looking answer where the real answer is unknown.

body.heading: Keep the map usable
paragraphs: The best first file is not the thickest one. It is the one with accurate directions, a clear access plan and someone who knows it exists. For the broader checklist, use [what to write down in case something happens](/guides/what-to-write-down-in-case-something-happens-to-you).

[Personal Life Affairs Companion](/shop/personal-life-affairs-companion) is an optional way to organise information you choose to record. It does not turn an information file into a will or grant authority. A protected folder and the free worksheet here are enough to begin.

sources.name: CaringInfo: advance directives by state and territory
sources.note: Advance-directive forms and requirements depend on location. An information file does not replace the appropriate legal documents.

used-car-no-service-records-what-to-do.title: Bought a used car with no service records? Start here
used-car-no-service-records-what-to-do.dek: Recover what you can, separate evidence from guesses, and agree a maintenance baseline with a mechanic. Missing paperwork is not a diagnosis.
used-car-no-service-records-what-to-do.metaDescription: Bought a used car with no service records? Find available history, check recalls, arrange an inspection and start a clear maintenance baseline.

paragraphs: If you bought a used car with no service records, ask the seller for receipts and previous service locations, write down today's mileage, check the correct owner's manual and arrange an independent mechanical inspection. Keep documented work separate from the seller's recollection. Start a record now, but do not treat the purchase date as the last service date.

The keys are yours. The history is not. Someone says it was always looked after, the glove box has an old handbook, and you are trying to decide whether the next bill is overdue maintenance or work that was done six months ago. The answer is not to assume everything is fine, or pay to replace everything. It is to find what can be established and make the remaining questions specific.

This guide is for US owners dealing with missing records. It helps you organise evidence and a conversation with a qualified mechanic; it does not diagnose the car or certify it safe to drive. If there are warning signs, damage or a known safety concern, follow the vehicle's warning instructions and seek appropriate professional help rather than waiting to finish the paperwork.

body.heading: The first five things to do
items: Record the VIN, year, model, engine or powertrain where known, current odometer reading and date. Check that the documents match the vehicle.
Ask the seller for invoices, digital records and the shops used. Keep the reply, but label recollections as reported rather than documented.
Get the manufacturer's manual and maintenance schedule for the correct year and version. Note any time-based and usage-based requirements rather than using a generic interval from another car.
Check official recall information and arrange an independent inspection. Explain that the maintenance history is incomplete and ask for a written priority list.
Agree what needs action, what needs further evidence, and what can be reviewed at a specific time or mileage. Recording a problem does not resolve a safety issue.

paragraphs: [Open the free used-car service baseline](/guides/print/library/used-car-no-service-records-what-to-do.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: Four evidence sources separate recorded service, reported history, recall information and present mechanical condition.
body.caption: A report, a receipt, a recall check and an inspection answer different questions.

body.heading: Where to look for a used car's service history
rows: The work, vehicle, date and mileage shown on an invoice
Everything that happened outside that record
Work recorded in that business's systems, if it can be released
Work done elsewhere or unrestricted access to a previous owner's personal information
Reported events, which may include service visits as well as title or damage information
A complete maintenance log or today's mechanical condition
Applicable recall information within that service's scope
That routine maintenance was done or that the whole vehicle is safe
Findings about the vehicle's current condition and recommended next steps
An exact past service date where there is no evidence

body.heading: Can CARFAX show oil changes and service records?
paragraphs: It can show reported services. [CARFAX describes](https://www.carfax.com/buying/how-to-read-a-carfax-report) maintenance entries such as oil changes and tire rotations. That does not mean every shop, owner or event appears. An empty entry is a gap in what you can see, not proof that the work never happened.

The [FTC explains](https://consumer.ftc.gov/features/feature-0040-used-cars) that vehicle-history products differ: title, loss and salvage data are not the same as a comprehensive service history. A history report does not replace an independent inspection. Use a report as one source and check what each entry actually says, rather than treating a clean-looking page as an all-clear.

body.heading: Give every maintenance fact an evidence label

left.label: What you can document
items: Invoice with the matching vehicle, work, date and mileage. Keep a copy and note anything unclear.
Your own new service receipt or the written findings from an inspection. Record what was done separately from what was recommended.

right.label: What still needs checking
items: Seller remembers a job but has no supporting record. Preserve their wording and its source; do not convert it into an exact service date.
No reliable information. Mark unknown and ask how to assess the risk for that item on this particular vehicle.

body.heading: Ask for a baseline, not a mystery full service

items.line: I bought this car with incomplete service records. Can you inspect its current condition, compare the unknown items with the correct manufacturer schedule, and give me written priorities before I authorise repairs?
Which items concern immediate safety, which are scheduled maintenance, and which are recommendations? What evidence supports each one, and what are the consequences of waiting?
Please give me the scope and price for the work requested today. Contact me for approval before adding work, and put the agreed next review date or mileage in writing.

body.heading: Do I need to replace every fluid and belt?
paragraphs: No blanket list can decide that from the absence of receipts. The model, age, actual condition, manufacturer instructions, use and evidence all matter. A timing belt is not interchangeable with a timing chain, and a photograph of a belt does not supply a reliable replacement history.

Ask the mechanic to identify the important unknowns and explain the appropriate assessment or service for each. Do not infer fluid condition or the correct work solely from colour, a seller's description or a generic internet interval. For each recommendation, keep the reason, urgency, quoted scope and what you authorised. The [mechanic conversation guide](/guides/what-to-tell-a-mechanic-before-work-starts) helps you keep that boundary clear.

body.alt: Three evidence states distinguish a documented invoice, a seller's reported memory and a genuinely unknown maintenance history.
body.caption: Unknown is not the same as never done, and it is not permission to ignore a safety concern.

body.heading: Check recalls without confusing them with maintenance
paragraphs: Use the [NHTSA recall lookup](https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls) for a US vehicle and follow any manufacturer instructions for a relevant recall. Read the lookup's limitations: repaired recalls, some newly announced recalls, certain older recalls, some manufacturers and international vehicles may not appear in the VIN result.

A zero result is not a full safety inspection. Save the result and date, and ask the manufacturer or dealer about anything unclear. A routine service recommendation, a safety recall and a service campaign are different things; ask which one you are discussing.

body.heading: A first entry that does not invent the past
body.intro: An invented example, not an inspection or a recommendation for a specific car.
rows: Bought 12 November; odometer 84,000 miles. This is the purchase reading, not a service date.
Seller says oil changes were regular; no receipts supplied.
One invoice found. Check VIN, actual work, date and mileage before treating it as relevant.
Previous timing-system service is unconfirmed. Mechanic to identify applicable system and manufacturer requirements.
Independent inspection booked. Written safety and maintenance priorities requested; repairs not yet authorised.

paragraphs: Once actual work is completed, add its date, mileage, shop and invoice reference. Keep recommendations and completed services in separate lines. The [car maintenance log guide](/guides/car-maintenance-log-what-to-write-down) shows what to keep, and the [manual schedule guide](/guides/car-maintenance-by-mileage-start-with-your-manual) helps you avoid transferring another model's intervals to yours.

body.heading: When the records do not turn up

items.q: Is buying a car with no service history always a mistake?
items.a: Missing records alone do not prove poor maintenance, but they leave uncertainty that paperwork cannot remove. If you have not bought yet, arrange an independent inspection before deciding. If you already own it, focus on a qualified assessment and a documented baseline, not on inventing a reassuring past.

items.q: Can a dealer find service history by VIN?
items.a: A dealer may have access to work recorded in its own or the manufacturer's systems, subject to availability and privacy rules. Ask what can be supplied for the vehicle and what it covers. A record from one network does not prove that no work happened at an independent shop.

items.q: Can I use the date I bought the car as the last service date?
items.a: No. Buying it establishes when you became the owner, not when oil, belts or other maintenance were last done. Record the purchase date separately. Use a documented service date when you have one, or keep the history unknown while agreeing the appropriate next action with a mechanic.

body.heading: Give the next owner a better starting point
paragraphs: A folder and a clear log are enough to begin. Keep what you can establish, label the rest, and add evidence as work happens. You are not trying to reconstruct every mile. You are trying to stop the next decision from starting with the same blank page.

If you want one place for the dates and intervals you actually know, [Vehicle Maintenance Companion](/shop/vehicle-maintenance-companion) is an optional tool. It supports unknown history and records you enter; it does not connect to your car, retrieve a VIN history, choose the real factory schedule or diagnose a problem. The guide and worksheet remain useful without buying it.

sources.name: FTC: Used Cars
sources.note: History-report scope, different providers and why a report does not replace an independent inspection.

sources.name: NHTSA: Check for Recalls
sources.note: VIN lookup and exclusions, including repaired recalls, some recent recalls, older recalls and international vehicles.

sources.name: CARFAX: How to Read a Report
sources.note: The provider describes reported oil changes and tire rotations; this corrects the earlier blanket claim that reports cannot include servicing.

what-goes-in-a-homeschool-portfolio.title: What goes in a homeschool portfolio? Keep the evidence
what-goes-in-a-homeschool-portfolio.dek: Choose dated work that explains what your child did and how learning developed. Build around the actual requirements, not a perfect-looking binder.
what-goes-in-a-homeschool-portfolio.metaDescription: Build a useful homeschool portfolio with a dated activity log, selected work and clear evidence notes. Check local requirements before submitting.

paragraphs: A homeschool portfolio brings together the records and work samples needed to explain a child's learning over a period. Depending on your rules and purpose, that may include an activity log, reading-material titles, dated writing or mathematics samples, project evidence and required assessment records. Start with the actual requirements, then select evidence that is understandable rather than merely attractive.

By the time you need the folder, the kitchen experiment has been cleared away and the best explanation happened out loud. A useful portfolio is built before those details disappear. It does not have to look like a published book. It has to make the work and its context findable.

This guide is for US parents assembling evidence for their own records or a requested review. Portfolio requirements differ by educational route, location and purpose. The suggestions below are an organisation method, not a promise that every authority requires or accepts the same contents.

body.heading: Find the purpose before choosing the pages
items: Identify whether this is a personal learning record, a required evaluation portfolio, a transfer record or another specific submission.
Locate the current official instructions for that purpose. Record required contents, deadlines, retention periods and who is entitled to request or receive material.
Choose a date range and keep one child's evidence identifiable. Do not mix several children's work without clear attribution.
Select dated items that show actual work and enough context to explain what the child did independently or with support.
Check that the log and samples agree. Keep gaps and reconstructed details visible rather than manufacturing a complete-looking history.

paragraphs: [Open the free homeschool portfolio evidence map](/guides/print/library/what-goes-in-a-homeschool-portfolio.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: Four portfolio evidence fields identify the work, its task, the help given and what changed or needs another check.
body.caption: Context makes a selected sample easier to understand.

body.heading: Choose evidence that answers a question
rows: A reading-title log, a short response or discussion note
What was read and what the child explained; not just a book-cover photo
Dated drafts or finished pieces from different points
The task, changes and any help given
Worked examples, problem-solving notes or an explanation
The idea being tested and the child's reasoning
Notes, drawings, measurements or a few relevant photographs
Question, method, observations and the child's contribution
The actual report or result required for your route
Date, provider and the requirement it fulfils

body.heading: Keep samples that explain progress, not just highlights
paragraphs: A polished final page may be useful, but it can hide the learning that got there. When appropriate, keep earlier and later examples with a brief note explaining the task. A sample corrected heavily by an adult should not be presented as wholly independent work.

You do not need to collect something impressive from every subject every week. Choose a manageable routine for saving useful evidence, alongside anything the applicable rules specifically require. The [learning-log template](/guides/homeschool-record-keeping-template) gives each sample a dated reference so you can find the supporting record.

Practical, oral and collaborative work can still be documented. A short note of what the child explained, a sketch or a photograph with context may preserve more information than a photograph of a completed object alone. Check what the particular review accepts; an attractive photo is not a substitute for required evidence.

body.heading: An invented portfolio entry with enough context
paragraphs: Suppose a child compares two seedlings over several weeks. The portfolio holds a dated drawing and measurement note, a photograph of the setup and a brief explanation of what the child noticed. The entry also says which parts were done together and which explanation the child gave without prompting.

The parent adds a later observation when the child changes the explanation. That pair tells a clearer story than a single picture labelled science project. It is still an example of documentation, not proof of a particular grade standard or a guarantee that an evaluator will accept those materials alone.

body.alt: A portfolio workflow distinguishes keeping required records, selecting evidence and making a specific submission.
body.caption: A working archive and a required submission do not have to be identical.

body.heading: Check local requirements without copying another family's rule
paragraphs: For a specific statutory example, [Florida's home-education law](https://wwwo.leg.state.fl.us/Statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=1000-1099%2F1002%2FSections%2F1002.41.html%2F) describes an activity log, reading-material titles and samples of student work. That is a Florida example, not a universal definition for every state or home-learning arrangement.

Use the [requirements verification guide](/guides/homeschool-record-keeping-requirements-by-state) to separate what must be retained from what must be submitted. Check current official instructions and ask for written clarification if requests conflict. Do not send private family information simply because it happens to be stored beside the learning records.

body.heading: Ask useful questions before an evaluation

items.line: Which portfolio contents are required for this review, what period should they cover, and where can I find the current written instructions?
Some learning was practical or discussed aloud. What form of dated observation or work evidence is appropriate for this process, and what additional records are required?

body.heading: Do one final evidence pass
items: Make dates, child names and subject references consistent enough that someone can follow them without your memory filling every gap.
Check that photographs and files open, that required originals are preserved, and that the review can use the format you chose.
Separate required submissions from personal working notes. Share only what is appropriate through the agreed route.
Save the submitted version and confirmation, then use [preparing for a homeschool evaluation](/guides/preparing-for-a-homeschool-evaluation) for the appointment or process itself.

body.heading: A portfolio does not have to be a showcase

items.q: How many samples should I keep for each subject?
items.a: There is no universal number. Start with the applicable rules and the purpose of the portfolio. Then choose enough relevant, dated evidence to explain the work and any development over time. A large stack of repetitive pages is not automatically more informative than a smaller set with clear context.

items.q: Can a homeschool portfolio be digital?
items.a: It can be useful digitally, but check the format accepted for the particular review and any rules about originals. Use understandable file names, dates, backups and access permissions. Make sure a reviewer can actually open the material before assuming a shared folder or a link is sufficient.

items.q: Should I leave mistakes out of the portfolio?
items.a: Not automatically. Earlier work and a later correction can explain learning, especially when the task and support are recorded. Select evidence for the portfolio's actual purpose, not to manufacture an appearance of perfect performance. Keep any specifically required materials even when they are not the pieces you would otherwise choose.

body.heading: Make the evidence easy to return to
paragraphs: The practical goal is a record you can explain and locate. Keep the [reading log](/guides/homeschool-reading-log), daily activity references and selected work connected instead of maintaining three unrelated archives.

[Homeschooling Companion](/shop/homeschooling-companion) is an optional place to organise the learning information you enter. It is not a curriculum, evaluator or legal certification. A clearly labelled folder and the free worksheet can do the first useful job without a purchase.

sources.name: Florida Legislature: section 1002.41, home education
sources.note: Official example of required activity-log and work-sample contents. These are Florida-specific requirements, not universal portfolio rules.

why-budgeting-apps-stop-working-after-tw.title: When your budgeting app stops working: a useful reset
why-budgeting-apps-stop-working-after-tw.dek: Before starting another budget, check whether the problem is stale data, too much upkeep, missing bills or income that does not cover the essentials.
why-budgeting-apps-stop-working-after-tw.metaDescription: Budgeting app no longer useful? Check data freshness, upkeep and missing commitments, then reset a small part of the plan without hiding the gap.

paragraphs: If your budgeting app has stopped being useful, identify the failure before replacing it: outdated transactions, excessive maintenance, missing commitments, unclear categories or income that does not cover the required costs. Restart with current balances and the bills due next, then restore only the detail you need. There is no evidence here for a universal two-month failure point.

The app opens with money left in a category, but you know the number cannot be right. Several purchases are uncategorised and an annual bill never made it into the plan. You close it, not because you stopped caring about money, but because this screen no longer answers a question you can trust.

That is one possible pattern, not a diagnosis of every abandoned budget. This guide is for someone deciding whether to repair an existing system or change it. It is not financial advice, and no app can close a real gap between reliable income and essential costs just by reorganising the categories.

body.heading: Find which part stopped helping
items: Check when balances and transactions were last updated. Separate missing data from money that is actually missing.
List essential payments due before the next reliable income, including non-monthly bills and known commitments.
Identify the maintenance job you stopped doing: imports, category decisions, manual entry, reconciliation or something else.
Choose one decision the budget should support this week, such as whether the next bills are covered. Do not rebuild every report first.
If essential costs exceed reliable income, deal with that problem directly and seek appropriate support rather than treating it as a software failure.

paragraphs: [Open the free budget app reset check](/guides/print/library/why-budgeting-apps-stop-working-after-two-months.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: Four budget problems distinguish stale information, maintenance effort, missing commitments and an actual income shortfall.
body.caption: A software reset is not the answer to every money problem.

body.heading: Different problems need different resets
rows: Account scope, duplicates, missing activity and update time
Compare a small current period with the underlying records
Which distinctions actually change a decision
Try fewer useful categories on a copy or a limited period
Add known non-monthly bills and dates before optional detail
The plan looks affordable but the week is not
Income and payment timing, not just monthly totals
Map what arrives and leaves before the next payday
The actual cost and income position
Prioritise essential needs and contact appropriate support

body.heading: Repair a trustworthy starting point
paragraphs: Start with the accounts you intend to include and note the date of the snapshot. Check pending activity and outstanding commitments rather than treating a higher balance as extra money. The [available versus current balance guide](/guides/available-balance-vs-current-balance) explains why the banking label still needs context.

If a backlog is large, you may decide to use a documented current starting point for planning while preserving old statements and any records needed for tax, disputes, reporting or other obligations. Do not erase required history just to make the app tidy. Write down what the reset includes and what remains unreconciled.

The [CFPB toolkit](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/educator-tools/your-money-your-goals/toolkit/) separates spending tracking, income, bill management and cash-flow tools. That is a useful distinction: a spending chart and a plan for paying next Tuesday's bill do not answer the same question.

body.heading: An invented reset after two missed weeks
paragraphs: A parent has two weeks of uncategorised activity and does not trust the remaining grocery figure. They do not assume the money is available, and they do not rebuild six months of reports before checking the rent. First they confirm current balances, expected income and the essential payments due before it arrives.

They then review the missing activity in a small, clearly defined period, watching for duplicates and forgotten bills. They reduce category choices that do not affect a decision, while preserving distinctions they actually need. The result is not proof that fewer categories work for everybody. It is a test of whether this particular system is maintainable.

body.alt: A three-stage budget reset establishes current information, checks upcoming commitments and tests a maintainable review process.
body.caption: Keep unresolved discrepancies visible instead of deleting them from the story.

body.heading: Test the system in an ordinary difficult week

left.label: Information worth protecting
items: Current balances with a known update time and a clear account scope.
Essential commitments, dates and reliable income timing.
Records that must be retained or checked, including unresolved discrepancies.

right.label: Detail that has to earn its upkeep
items: Category splits that never change what you decide.
Reports you create but do not use.
Repeated entry or sorting that makes the core information harder to keep current.

body.heading: Make the review concrete

items.line: Which balances and bills need to be current for our next decision, who will check them, and when will we compare the result with the source records?
Before moving everything, I want to test one normal week: adding activity, seeing what is due, finding errors and returning after a missed update. I will keep the existing records while I test.

body.heading: Before moving to another budgeting app
items: Check export, deletion, data access and saving arrangements. Keep records you need independently of a subscription.
Test how the tool handles a missed week and a non-monthly bill, not only a perfectly entered first day.
Confirm whether imports or connections are supported and what requires manual checking. An automatic feed is not automatic understanding.

Choose a review routine that fits your actual responsibilities. Use [starting over after budget failure](/guides/how-to-start-over-after-budget-failure) for the broader restart, rather than repeatedly redesigning this one screen.

body.heading: A reset without another grand promise

items.q: Do budgeting apps always fail after two months?
items.a: No universal timeline is established here. People stop using tools for different reasons, including practical workload, changing circumstances and a poor fit with the decision they need to make. Look at your own point of failure rather than treating a particular week or month as an inevitable pattern.

items.q: Should I delete the budget and start again?
items.a: Not automatically. Preserve statements and records needed for reporting, disputes or other obligations. You can create a clearly dated current planning baseline without pretending older discrepancies are resolved. If you change tools, check export and saving arrangements before removing the original information.

items.q: Will fewer categories fix the problem?
items.a: They may reduce maintenance if the current distinctions are not useful, but they do not fix missing transactions, incorrect balances or insufficient income. Keep distinctions needed for real decisions and obligations. Test a simpler structure on a small period before changing everything or assuming simplicity alone makes a plan accurate.

body.heading: Keep the budget's job small enough to trust
paragraphs: The useful result is not a more impressive dashboard. It is a reliable answer to the next financial question, with gaps visible rather than hidden. Our [monthly bills list](/guides/monthly-bills-list) and [end-of-month review](/guides/end-of-month-money-review) cover two specific jobs that should not depend on a perfect category system.

[Personal Finance Companion](/shop/personal-finance-companion) is an optional product to assess against those needs. No product can promise that you will maintain it or that your income will cover your costs. The free reset sheet lets you test the approach before buying anything.

sources.name: CFPB: Your Money, Your Goals toolkit
sources.note: Provides separate tools for spending, income, bills and cash-flow planning. Does not establish a universal app-abandonment timeline.

why-to-do-lists-make-it-worse.title: Why your to-do list feels overwhelming: change the job
why-to-do-lists-make-it-worse.dek: A list can store everything you owe yourself and still leave you unable to start. Separate the backlog from today's next action before adding another app.
why-to-do-lists-make-it-worse.metaDescription: To-do list overwhelming you? Separate the backlog from a clear next action, real deadlines and blocked work. Reset one item without rewriting everything.

paragraphs: If your to-do list feels overwhelming, check whether it is trying to be a backlog, a decision-maker, a calendar and a set of instructions at the same time. Keep the full record somewhere findable, then choose one useful next action and keep real deadlines visible. You do not have to rewrite the whole list before starting.

Taxes. Dentist. Mum's birthday. Fix the car. Those are useful reminders that something exists. They are not yet instructions you can follow. When every glance requires you to decide the priority, remember the context and work out the first move, looking at the list can become another task.

This is an organisational experiment, not a diagnosis or a treatment for ADHD, anxiety or other conditions. Lists help many people; feeling stuck does not prove a particular cause. If difficulties are persistent or affecting daily life, seek appropriate support rather than assuming a better planner must solve everything.

body.heading: Reset one item, not the whole backlog
items: Choose one item that matters today. Check actual deadlines and consequences before picking the easiest item by default.
Rewrite it as a visible action you can take: open, find, ask, compare, send or book, with the object named.
Put the information needed for that action beside it, such as the document location, contact or booking reference.
If the action depends on someone else, record who you are waiting for and when to review it. Do not keep calling it today's task if you cannot advance it.
Keep the rest of the backlog available but outside this immediate view. Make a deliberate review time so out of sight does not become forgotten.

paragraphs: [Open the free overwhelming to-do list reset](/guides/print/library/why-to-do-lists-make-it-worse.html). Use the worksheet without an account or purchase.

body.alt: Four task categories distinguish the backlog, next action, actual deadline and waiting work instead of mixing them into one urgent list.
body.caption: A clear action view can coexist with a complete record.

body.heading: A reminder and an action are different things
body.intro: Invented examples. The right action depends on your situation and any real deadlines.
columns: What needs to be beside it
rows: Find the clinic's current appointment contact
Clinic name and any relevant appointment instructions
Open the last provider reply and identify the requested document
Booking reference and the provider's message
Locate the notice and read the actual deadline
Notice, account access route and adviser contact if needed
Send the inspection findings to the chosen mechanic and ask for scope
Vehicle details and the written findings

body.heading: Do not make everything due today
paragraphs: A date can mean a deadline, a planned session or a reminder to check something. If every row says today, you lose that distinction. Keep real deadlines explicit. Put a review date on waiting work and an intended time on work you actually plan to do.

That is not permission to ignore an overdue bill or official notice. If the consequences are already active, the next step may be to contact the relevant organisation or get qualified help, not spend the morning reformatting the list. Use [starting when everything is overdue](/guides/how-to-start-when-everything-is-overdue) for triage rather than applying a gentle backlog reset to an urgent situation.

body.heading: Give different kinds of work different places

left.label: Available to do
items: One selected action with the information needed to start.
A real deadline or planned time, clearly distinguished from a vague wish.

right.label: Not an action for right now
items: A backlog item you intend to reconsider, with a review arrangement.
Waiting work with the person or missing information identified.

body.alt: A three-step reset identifies an obligation, a visible first move and any practical obstacle that still prevents action.
body.caption: Difficulty starting is not a diagnosis and does not have one universal cause.

body.heading: A first move can reveal a different obstacle
paragraphs: Sometimes the action is clear and you still cannot start. You may lack time, money, permission, energy or a decision. You may be worried about the result. A smaller verb cannot remove every barrier, and that does not make the method or the person a failure.

An invented example: Rowan changes insurance to 'open the renewal letter'. Once it is open, the obstacle is not remembering where to click. The quote is unaffordable. The next task becomes understanding the options or seeking advice, not creating a more elaborate reminder to renew.

If this is the recurring pattern, [thinking about a task without doing it](/guides/why-you-keep-thinking-about-a-task-and-not-doing-it) explores the decision bottleneck, while [the ten-minute task-paralysis guide](/guides/task-paralysis-what-to-do-in-the-next-ten-minutes) focuses on a short attempt at starting. Neither should be presented as a clinical explanation for every reader.

body.heading: Ask for specific help

items.line: Can you stay with me while I open this and identify what is being asked? I do not need you to take it over; I need help finding the next decision.
I cannot complete this until I have the missing information. Can you tell me who provides it, what you need from me, and the date I should follow up?

body.heading: A tool is allowed to help without explaining you
paragraphs: The [East London NHS support page](https://www.elft.nhs.uk/adult-adhd-services/support-available) includes task and organisation resources among wider support options. That is a useful counterweight to the claim that lists are inherently bad. A particular format can help one person and create extra work for another.

Try this reset on a small part of your existing system before moving everything into a new app. Judge whether you can find the action, the necessary information and the follow-up. A tidy screenshot is not the measure of whether a tool fits your day.

body.heading: When the list is still difficult

items.q: Does struggling with a to-do list mean I have ADHD?
items.a: No. A list problem alone cannot diagnose ADHD or any other condition. There are many possible practical and personal reasons a task may be difficult. If attention, organisation or starting difficulties are persistent and affect daily life, discuss the broader pattern with an appropriate qualified professional.

items.q: Should I delete my backlog to feel less overwhelmed?
items.a: Not automatically. Deleting everything can also remove real obligations and useful context. Separate the immediate action view from the stored backlog, preserve important deadlines and make a review arrangement. Remove outdated items deliberately rather than using deletion as a substitute for checking whether something still matters.

items.q: What if even the first small action feels impossible?
items.a: Check what is making it unavailable: missing information, a decision, cost, time, energy or distress. The appropriate next step may be asking for support or clarifying the problem, not making the action smaller forever. Use urgent or professional help appropriate to the actual circumstances rather than relying on a list technique.

body.heading: A list with a smaller job
paragraphs: Keep the obligations. Give today's action a clearer place. The free reset sheet asks what matters, what can move, what is blocked and when the rest will be reviewed.

[ADHD Life Companion](/shop/adhd-life-companion) is an optional product to consider if its approach suits you. It is not a diagnosis or treatment, and no product is required for the method here. Start with one useful action, not a promise to become a different kind of person.

sources.name: East London NHS Foundation Trust: adult ADHD support resources
sources.note: Support resources include organisation and task tools. This does not establish that to-do lists cause ADHD symptoms or that one method works for everyone.
